clue.text: Moody Maureen got out of bed

parts.note: Mo is a common short form of the name Maureen
to get out of bed is to rise, past tense rose

explanation.surface: A woman called Maureen climbs out of bed in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone morose is sullen and gloomy, which is what a moody person often is.

clue.text: Loose men terribly in need of company?

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the two words are badly jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Some unattached men wander about badly wanting companionship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' signals the anagram of LOOSE MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely person longs for companions, so the question-marked phrase describes that feeling.

clue.text: Dawn working hard to bring fresh hope for the economy?

parts.note: dawn is daybreak, when the sun comes up
diligent hard work is called industry

explanation.surface: A new day of diligent labour might revive a flagging national economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A new, fast-growing business sector is called this, a promise of economic growth.

clue.text: Once again locks up fellow among left-wingers

indicators.note: among places the fellow within the group of left-wingers

parts.note: communists or socialists are informally reds
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone jails a man who mixes with leftist radicals, and does it repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that sends an accused person back into custody pending trial is said to do this.

clue.text: Graduate briefly employed by Birmingham school

parts.note: the abbreviated degree is tucked inside the words Birmingham school, across the end of one and start of the other

explanation.surface: A postgraduate takes a job at a school in Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of BirminghaM and start of SChool give MSc, and 'briefly' says that is only the abbreviation: the entry is the degree spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of this postgraduate degree is a graduate, the qualification standing for the person.

clue.text: It's correct to go after loud alarm

indicators.note: to go after says the word for correct follows the letter for loud

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
correct means right

explanation.surface: Someone says it is proper for a noisy warning to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm here is a noun meaning sudden fear or shock, a synonym.

clue.text: Murderer in hut, concealing body initially

indicators.note: concealing hides the letter away so it no longer shows in the word for hut

parts.note: a cabin is a small hut

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of body

explanation.surface: A killer hides in a shack with the corpse of his victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' here means making the B vanish from CABIN, not wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the elder son of Adam and Eve killed his brother Abel, the first murderer.

clue.text: Ferry soldiers back repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly calls for the reversed pair twice in a row
back says the letters for soldiers are read in reverse

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops return again and again by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-on roll-off vessel is a type of car ferry, abbreviated with this hyphenated form.

clue.text: Ellington? Not his first instrument!

indicators.note: not his first means the jazzman's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Duke Ellington was the famous American jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: A remark that this was not the jazz bandleader's first instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The ukulele, a small four-stringed guitar, is shortened to this form.

clue.text: An examination in a chamber

parts.note: a trial is a test or examination

explanation.surface: A test conducted inside a room or judge's chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to an atrium, a chamber of the heart, so it describes what lies in a chamber.

clue.text: Problem involving upper-class person acting insincerely

indicators.note: involving means the word for problem wraps around the class letter

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling problem
U is the standard label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A dilemma involving a posh person who puts on false airs.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious type who affects attitudes to impress others is a show-off of this kind.

clue.text: Mythical daughter, opponent no longer with us

parts.note: an anti is someone opposed to something
a euphemism for dead or departed, i.e. gone

explanation.surface: A legendary woman whose adversary has died.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Oedipus's daughter, heroine of Sophocles' tragedy, bears this name.

clue.text: Fresh thought about helping to restrict opposing team

parts.note: re means about or concerning
con means against, as in pros and cons
a side is a team
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A rethink about a portion size meant to hold back the rival team.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking something over again yields new thought on it, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Cells seen as round with very small area

parts.note: a round shape resembles the letter O
a, a small letter, is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Microscope cells seem circular and occupy a tiny space.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs, the female reproductive cells, are called by this Latin plural.

clue.text: Country fellows settling in a sort of valley

indicators.note: settling in places the fellows within the valley word

parts.note: a ria is a drowned river valley
fellows are men

explanation.surface: Men make their homes in a particular kind of valley in some country.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caucasus republic, once part of the USSR, is a nation of this name.

clue.text: Revolutionary member of political party mostly offering nonsense

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning the remaining letters round
mostly means the party member's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A radical within a party speaks rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TORY to TOR, and 'Revolutionary' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is informal for rubbish or drivel, a straight synonym of nonsense.

clue.text: Eccentric, like policeman who has finished duty?

definitions.text: like policeman who has finished duty?
definitions.meaning: a constable no longer walking his patrol route is away from his rounds

explanation.surface: A quirky description of a constable whose shift has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric and unconventional are synonyms; read in two parts it describes a patrol officer done with his round.

clue.text: Bishop came down hard on diocese with casual attitude?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to alight is to land, past tense lit
H stands for hard, as on pencils
Ely is an English cathedral city and diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop cracked down on his diocese in a careless manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carefree and without concern is doing it lightly and cheerfully, a synonym.

clue.text: Deep down that somehow engages listener

indicators.note: engages means the jumbled letters take in the organ of hearing
somehow suggests the letters of that are arranged in some other way

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Something that grabs a hearer's attention at a profound level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes ATHT, which 'engages' (holds) the organ of hearing; 'listener' looks like a person but is the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fundamentally or in one's true nature, the same as deep down.

clue.text: Severest edict to upset employees in shops

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A harsh decree is issued to annoy shop staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals the anagram; note that 'to' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain-clothes staff hired to catch shoplifters work inside retail premises.

clue.text: Sartre turned out to be most unusual

indicators.note: turned out suggests the philosopher's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: The French philosopher proved to be a highly unusual figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' signals the anagram of SARTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of rare means least common, so most unusual.

clue.text: Girl from French city undermining continental community

indicators.note: undermining places the city beneath the community in this down entry

parts.note: EU is the European Union
Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A woman from the Riviera city who is subverting the European bloc.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Game that gets the French going round a monument?

indicators.note: going round means the French article wraps the other letters

parts.note: le is a French form of the definite article
a cross is a monument, as on a grave or the Eleanor crosses

explanation.surface: A sport in which French visitors run circles round a memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' tempts as LA since the answer starts that way, but it is the masculine article, going round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A field sport played with netted sticks, originating among Native Americans, is a team game.

clue.text: Plant on a wall pruned and growing upwards

indicators.note: growing upwards means the letters run bottom to top in this down entry
pruned means the wall word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a mural is something painted on a wall; as an adjective it means on a wall

explanation.surface: A plant trained along a wall is cut back and grows upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pruned' cuts MURAL to MURA; 'growing upwards' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily, or lords-and-ladies, is a genus of flowering plant.

clue.text: Gas supplying energy to most of Kent region

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: most of means the region's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Thanet is an area of north-east Kent

explanation.surface: A gas company supplies power to much of a Kent district.
explanation.walkthrough: THANET is a district of Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless flammable hydrocarbon found in natural gas is named this.

clue.text: Scoundrels against Her Majesty — one swears

parts.note: curs are contemptible men, scoundrels
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Villains opposed to the Queen, one of whom uses foul language.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who utters oaths or profanities is one who curses.

clue.text: Big bird from Cornwall heading west

indicators.note: heading west means the letters run right to left in this across entry
from says the letters come out of the word Cornwall

explanation.surface: A large bird flies west out of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes COR from Cornwall; 'heading west' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabian legend a giant bird of prey able to carry off elephants bears this name.

clue.text: Secure hair

definitions.meaning: to fasten firmly with a key
a tress or ringlet of hair

explanation.surface: Fasten your hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten shut is one sense; a tress or curl of hair is another.
